title: Transient pegging and deceleration backoff for fast-path handshake
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a runtime mechanism that temporarily 'pegs' a fast-path model for the prefill + early decode handshake and applies a deceleration/backoff controller to reduce oscillation and rollback churn. Goal: increase fast-path acceptance rate without increasing incorrect-accept rollbacks or tail latency. This ticket covers design, perf microbenchmarks, a conservative canary rollout, and operational thresholds for automatic fallback to stable decode paths.
acceptance_criteria: Fast-path acceptance rate increases by >=8% on benchmark conversational workload compared to current baseline with no pegging
False-accept (rollback) rate does not increase by more than 1 percentage point
P95 decode latency remains within 5% of baseline; P99 increase capped at 10ms for the canary population
Canary rollout automation triggers rollback if rollback frequency > 0.7% for 5m or if error rate spike > 2x
Unit and integration tests for handshake state transitions and backoff logic exist and pass in CI
design_notes: Motivation: current speculative-like fast-paths switch models during the prefill->decode boundary and sometimes oscillate under mixed-frequency workloads, causing repeated rollbacks and cache thrash.

Transient pegging: on prefill probe success, peg the chosen fast-path model for the next N tokens (configurable, default 4). Pegging avoids immediate model re-evaluation during steady short responses.

Deceleration/backoff controller: when a pegged model causes a rollback, increase backoff window exponentially for subsequent requests from that client/session; decay backoff over time and successful accepts.
Kernel-awareness: prefer pegging candidates whose kernel fingerprint matches the current runtime (e.g., fp16 fused attention kernels) to reduce cache and kernel-switch cost during quick handoffs.
Acceptance score smoothing: apply an EWMA on acceptance scores per kernel/model pair to avoid noise-driven decisions; per-tenant smoothing factor configurable.
Telemetry: emit acceptance.decayed_score, pegged_model_id, peg_duration, backoff_seconds, rollback_reason and kernel_fingerprint tags for analysis.
Safety: pegging is disabled for sessions marked high-safety or long-running streaming flows; RBAC-enabled customers can opt-out in Private deployments.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design + simulation): implement a simulator that replays recent traffic (token-level traces) to evaluate pegging windows 1..8 and backoff policies (fixed vs exponential).
Phase 2 (runtime prototype): add lightweight peg state to request context and selection logic in the router; add backoff table keyed by session_id / client_id with TTL and jitter.
Phase 3 (integration): integrate kernel_fingerprint into router heuristics; add EWMA acceptance store and expose in local metrics.
Phase 4 (canary rollout): 1% of traffic in a canary region; automated alarms and rollback hooks wired into console/monitoring.
Phase 5 (analysis + tuning): collect telemetry for 72h, analyze false-accept vs cost delta, tune defaults and land RFC for wider rollout.
tests: Unit tests for peg lifecycle: create->extend->evict->decay
Integration test: synthetic workload with model flapping to ensure backoff stabilizes routing
Perf microbench: single-node latency and throughput with and without pegging across common model families
Chaos test: forced kernel mismatch path to ensure graceful fallback and correct metrics emission
Canary gating test: alarm triggers on rollback rate > threshold and executes rollback hook
